question: Which SDLC phase comes immediately after Requirements Analysis?
feedback: Design turns the agreed requirements into an architecture and detailed plan before coding starts.

question: What is the main purpose of the Planning phase?
option2: Deciding scope, budget, schedule and feasibility
feedback: Planning decides what will be built, with what resources and by when.

question: In the Waterfall model, how easy is it to change requirements late in the project?
option3: Hard and costly because phases are sequential
feedback: Waterfall finishes each phase before the next starts, so late changes cause expensive rework.

question: Which statement about Agile is correct?
option1: Requirements are frozen at the start
option2: Work is delivered in short iterations with regular feedback
option3: Testing happens only at the end
option4: Documentation is the only measure of progress
feedback: Agile delivers working software in short cycles and adapts to feedback.

question: Who orders the Product Backlog in Scrum?
feedback: The Product Owner maximises product value by ordering the backlog.

question: What is a Sprint in Scrum?
option2: A time-boxed iteration of 1 to 4 weeks
feedback: A Sprint is a fixed-length iteration in which a usable increment is produced.

question: A team needs a short daily sync about progress and blockers. Which Scrum event is this?
feedback: The Daily Scrum is a 15-minute event for the Developers to plan the next day of work.

question: What does the Maintenance phase involve?
option2: Fixing defects and updating the software after release
feedback: Maintenance keeps the released software working and up to date.

question: What does CI stand for in CI/CD?
feedback: Continuous Integration means merging code often and building and testing it automatically.

question: On a Kanban board, which column holds a story someone is actively working on?
feedback: Work that has started but is not finished sits in In Progress.

question: Which phase turns approved requirements into a system architecture and detailed plan?
feedback: The Design phase defines how the system will be built.

question: Which activity belongs to the Testing phase?
option2: Verifying the software against requirements and finding defects
feedback: Testing checks that the software meets the requirements and finds defects.

question: A system has fixed, well-understood regulatory requirements. Which model fits well?
feedback: Stable and well-understood requirements suit a plan-driven approach such as Waterfall.

question: Which is a core value of the Agile Manifesto?
option3: Responding to change over following a plan
feedback: Agile values responding to change over following a plan.

question: Who helps the team follow Scrum and removes impediments?
feedback: The Scrum Master serves the team by coaching Scrum and removing obstacles.

question: What is the Sprint Retrospective for?
option3: Inspecting how the team worked and agreeing improvements
feedback: The Retrospective focuses on improving the team's way of working.

question: At the end of a Sprint the team shows the working increment to stakeholders. Which event is this?
feedback: The Sprint Review inspects the increment and gathers feedback.

question: In a CI/CD pipeline, what normally happens right after the code is built?
option2: The release goes straight to customers
feedback: Automated tests validate the build before it moves further down the pipeline.

question: What does Continuous Delivery mean?
option2: Code is always kept in a releasable state through an automated pipeline
feedback: Continuous Delivery keeps every change ready to be released through automation.

question: Which Kanban practice limits the amount of unfinished work?
feedback: A work-in-progress limit stops the team from starting too many items at once.

question: A start-up expects customer needs to change every few weeks and wants early feedback. Which approach suits best?
feedback: Frequent change and early feedback are exactly what short Agile sprints support.

question: A client demands a fixed contract with a detailed signed specification up front. Which model is the most natural fit?
feedback: A fixed, fully specified scope favours the plan-driven Waterfall approach.

question: Your team keeps finding bugs only after release. Which CI/CD improvement helps most?
option1: Add automated tests to the pipeline
feedback: Automated tests in the pipeline catch defects before they reach users.

question: In Sprint 3 the team finds that a key requirement was misunderstood. What is the Agile response?
option1: Ignore it until the project ends
option2: Update the Product Backlog and adjust in the next Sprint
feedback: Agile welcomes change: the backlog is updated and the next Sprint adapts.

question: Two developers edit the same file and the build breaks after merging. Which practice would have caught this earlier?
option2: Continuous Integration with frequent merges and builds
feedback: Frequent integration with automated builds exposes conflicts early.

question: A team wants to visualise work states and limit work in progress without fixed-length iterations. Which method fits?
feedback: Kanban visualises flow on a board and limits work in progress.
